case_title: Roopsena Khatun v. State of West Bengal
confession: Extra-judicial confession, but not relied on
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and Section 379 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused drowned the victim in a pond and removed a silver chain from her body. The victim went missing after leaving her house for her grandmother's house. A witness claimed to have seen the victim following the accused. The accused was apprehended by villagers the next day and allegedly confessed to the crime. The prosecution relied on the accused's disclosure, an extra-judicial confession, the recovery of a silver chain from the accused, and the last seen circumstance. The body of the victim was found floating in the pond the day after she went missing. The prosecution did not establish the time of death or the exact manner of the victim's death. The accused was described as a young girl, and there were questions about her age and the possibility of accidental drowning.
